what_is_wrong: Creating an asset with a category_id or vendor_id that does not exist returns an unhandled 500 instead of a clean 4xx. The handler DOES have a DBAPIError guard that converts constraint failures into a client error, but it only wraps db.commit(); the row is written by an db.flush() that runs BEFORE the try block, and the FK check fires on that INSERT, so the exception escapes the guard entirely. Sibling endpoints in the same router (asset-request create, maintenance create) return a clean 4xx for the same class of error, so a 4xx is clearly the intended behavior. Server state is rolled back correctly - this is purely an error-handling defect, not corruption.
suspected_cause: app/api/v1/assets.py:249 - `await db.flush()` sits outside the `try:` at line 256 whose `except DBAPIError` at 258-260 calls `_as_client_error(exc, "Rejected by a database constraint")`

what_is_wrong: Assigning an asset to an employee_id that does not exist returns an unhandled 500. Unlike create/update, assign_asset has NO try/except DBAPIError around its commit at all, so the FK violation propagates as an unhandled exception. POST /api/v1/assets/{asset_id}/transfer has the identical code shape and the identical 500. Rollback is clean (asset stays IN_STORE / previous holder retained), so this is an error-handling defect only.
suspected_cause: app/api/v1/assets.py:505 (assign_asset) and app/api/v1/assets.py:538 (transfer_asset) - bare `await db.commit()` with no `except DBAPIError` handler

status_observed: 200 OK, but the assignment-history table it writes accumulates duplicate and permanently-open rows
what_is_wrong: Unassigning writes duplicate UNASSIGNED history rows and leaves them open forever. _unassign loops over every history row with to_date IS NULL and, for EACH one, closes it AND inserts a new UNASSIGNED row - but the UNASSIGNED rows it creates are themselves written with to_date = NULL, and assign_asset never closes them. So every assign/unassign cycle leaves one more permanently-open row behind, and the next unassign emits one new UNASSIGNED row per open row. After N cycles the asset has N open rows and N*(N+1)/2 UNASSIGNED rows instead of N. GET /assets/{id}/assignment-history therefore reports an audit trail that is factually wrong: it shows the asset being handed back several times for a single hand-back. The same code path is reached by POST /assets/{asset_id}/reclaim with working_condition=true, which calls _unassign. This also feeds GET /employees/me/assets, whose assigned_date_from/assigned_date_to filter selects history rows by `to_date IS NULL` and will match these stale UNASSIGNED rows.
suspected_cause: app/api/v1/assets.py:552-560 - _unassign creates the new AssetAssignmentHistory(action="UNASSIGNED") INSIDE the `for hist in ... to_date.is_(None)` loop and gives it no to_date; app/api/v1/assets.py:500 (assign_asset) never closes pre-existing open rows

status_observed: 200, with a RETIRED_DISPOSED asset listed inside due_soon
what_is_wrong: The "warranty or maintenance due soon" section of the summary report is built from all filtered assets with no status exclusion, so an asset that is already RETIRED_DISPOSED is reported as having maintenance due soon - while the very same response separately counts it under retired_count. Operationally a disposed asset cannot need upcoming maintenance, so the due_soon list overstates work outstanding. What I could NOT prove: I have no spec text stating retired assets must be excluded from this section, so I cannot rule out that listing them is deliberate. Related and possibly the same root gap: POST /assets/{asset_id}/maintenance has no status guard and accepts a new maintenance log with a future next_due_date against an already-retired asset (201), which is how an asset lands in this state.
